environment.postgresql: PostgreSQL 18.3 server (local, port 54329, user postgres, trust authentication), psql 18.3; password-authentication runs used a second local 18.3 server with scram-sha-256

procedure: Exported the lab files of the named commit with git archive into uncommitted private staging outside the repository.
Ran the setup command mvn -q dependency:go-offline in starter/ against an empty local Maven repository.
Created an unrelated database named relational_design_lab (the old fixed lab name) holding a marker table, then ran mvn -q -o test on the shipped starter.

Replaced only starter/schema.sql with the privately staged completed schema; the public tests were byte-identical to the commit; ran mvn -q -o test again with PGHOST, PGPORT and PGUSER pointing at the local server.

Ran the same command with a privately staged alternative suitable schema (bigint identity id, text name with a length CHECK, varchar email and code, smallint capacity, timestamptz DEFAULT now(), numeric(10,2) grade, UNIQUE pair instead of a primary key, ON DELETE RESTRICT) and with three nonconforming task-5 schemas (constant 2000-01-01 default, nullable enrolled_at, numeric grade without scale).
result: Completed schema: mvn -q -o test exited 0 with empty stdout (stderr held only JDK/Maven native-access warnings); surefire report: Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0.
starterRun: On the shipped starter, mvn -q -o test exits 1 and fails all five declared failingTests (Tests run: 5, Failures: 5), each with a stable message naming the missing table or column.
cleanup: Every run created only starter/target inside the lab and one uniquely named relational_design_lab_<12 hex> database, which it dropped at the end; afterwards no relational_design_lab_% database remained and starter/target/lab-database.txt was gone. The marker database was then dropped by the author and starter/target deleted, leaving no lab database.
otherSystems: Password authentication was run on macOS against a scram-sha-256 server: through a PGPASSFILE password file (exit 0, 5 passed), with no password available (stable 'Could not reach PostgreSQL' setup error), and through PGPASSWORD (exit 0, 5 passed); a socket-directory PGHOST gave the stable 'PGHOST is set to ... which is not a host name' error. Linux and Windows runs are not yet recorded and remain unverified; CI covers Ubuntu (lab-contract section 10).
testScope: The public tests check table and column names, that each column's type is a suitable kind for its criterion, which inserts and deletes PostgreSQL accepts or rejects (by SQLSTATE), and the values it stores (current-time default, exact two-decimal grade); they do not check constraint names, statement layout or one particular type spelling.
variantRuns: Alternative suitable schema: exit 0, Tests run: 5, Failures: 0. Each nonconforming task-5 schema: exit 1 with only task5EnrollmentDefaults failing (Tests run: 5, Failures: 1).
collisionSafety: The pre-existing relational_design_lab database and its marker row (42) survived the starter, completed, alternative and nonconforming runs. In a separate private run with the name generator forced to collide on its first attempt, a pre-created relational_design_lab_000000000000 database with a marker survived and the run used a second generated name (Tests run: 5, Failures: 0).
